parts.label: (a)
key_concepts: isolated system with no resultant external force
hints: Hint 1: Think about the total momentum of all the objects interacting together, comparing the situation just before and just after they interact.
Hint 2: Remember this constancy is only guaranteed under a special condition about outside influences - what must be true about any external resultant force?
parts.proper_answer: The total momentum of a system of bodies remains constant, so total momentum before equals total momentum after, provided there is no resultant external force acting on the system.
walkthrough:
Step 1: **What is conserved**
Momentum is mass times velocity, and it is a vector. For two colliding balls, you do not look at each ball alone. You add their momenta together to get the total momentum of the system. In the absence of outside pushes, that total cannot be created or destroyed, only shared between the balls.

Step 2: **The vital condition**
This sharing rule only holds for an isolated system. That means no resultant external force acts, so friction, gravity and other outside impulses are zero or cancel. Internal forces during the collision are equal and opposite and cancel out, leaving $$p_{total\,before} = p_{total\,after}$$

parts.label: (b)(i)
hints: Hint 1: Start by comparing the total momentum before the collision, where only ball X is moving, with the total momentum after, where only ball Y is moving.
walkthrough:
Step 1: **Set total before equal to total after**
Ball Y starts at rest, so all the initial momentum is carried by X. After, ball X is at rest, so all the momentum is carried by Y. Using $$m_X u_X = m_Y v_Y$$ gives $$240 \times 16 = 480 \times v$$

Step 2: **Solve for v**
$$v = \frac{240 \times 16}{480} = 8.0\text{ m s}^{-1}$$ Masses can stay in grams here because the same unit appears on both sides and cancels.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
hints: Hint 1: Recall how kinetic energy depends on mass and speed, and note that momentum can be conserved while kinetic energy is not.
Hint 2: Calculate the total kinetic energy before using the mass of X in kg and speed 16 m s-1, then calculate the total after using the mass of Y in kg and speed 8.0 m s-1.
Hint 3: Subtract final from initial, or find initial minus final, to get the loss due to the collision.
parts.proper_answer: $\Delta E_K = 15\text{ J}$ loss, from $30.7\text{ J}$ before to $15.4\text{ J}$ after.
walkthrough:
Step 1: **Kinetic energy formula**
Kinetic energy is scalar and given by $$E_K = \frac{1}{2}mv^2$$ You need mass in kg for joules, so $240\text{ g} = 0.24\text{ kg}$ and $480\text{ g} = 0.48\text{ kg}$.

Step 2: **Energy before and after**
Before, only X moves: $$E_{K,before} = \frac{1}{2} \times 0.24 \times 16^2 = 30.72\text{ J}$$ After, only Y moves: $$E_{K,after} = \frac{1}{2} \times 0.48 \times 8.0^2 = 15.36\text{ J}$$

Step 3: **Change due to collision**
$$\Delta E_K = E_{K,before} - E_{K,after} = 30.72 - 15.36 \approx 15\text{ J}$$ The total decreases, so the collision is inelastic. Lost energy goes to sound, heat and permanent deformation.

parts.label: (c)(i)
key_concepts: force equals rate of change of momentum
hints: Hint 1: Think of force as how quickly momentum changes during the short contact time, so focus on the change in momentum of ball X.
Hint 2: Work out the initial momentum of ball X to the right and its final momentum of zero, then find the size of the change.
Hint 3: Convert 2.0 ms to seconds and divide the momentum change by this time, then decide which way ball Y must push on X to stop it.
parts.proper_answer: $F = 1900\text{ N}$ (to 2 s.f.) acting to the left on ball X.
walkthrough:
Step 1: **Link force to momentum change**
Impulse equals change in momentum: $$F\Delta t = \Delta p = m\Delta v$$ For ball X, velocity goes from $+16\text{ m s}^{-1}$ to zero in $\Delta t = 2.0\text{ ms} = 2.0 \times 10^{-3}\text{ s}$.

Step 2: **Calculate magnitude**
Change in magnitude of momentum of X: $$\Delta p = 0.24 \times 16 = 3.84\text{ kg m s}^{-1}$$ Hence $$F = \frac{\Delta p}{\Delta t} = \frac{3.84}{2.0 \times 10^{-3}} = 1920\text{ N} \approx 1900\text{ N}$$ You get the same result using ball Y gaining $0.48 \times 8.0$ of momentum in the same time.

Step 3: **Decide direction**
Ball X was moving to the right and is brought to rest, so its momentum decreases to the right. The force from Y must oppose the motion, acting to the left to produce a leftward impulse.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
hints: Hint 1: Think about the fundamental law that links the force of X on Y to the force of Y on X when two bodies are in contact.
Hint 2: Recall what that law says about the sizes of the two forces and about their directions along the same line.
parts.proper_answer: The force on Y by X has equal magnitude to that in (c)(i) but opposite direction, i.e. to the right.
walkthrough:
Step 1: **Newton's third law pair**
When two bodies interact, they exert equal and opposite forces on each other at the same time. The force on X by Y and the force on Y by X form such a pair.

Step 2: **Apply to this collision**
So magnitude is the same, about $1900\text{ N}$, but direction is reversed. If Y pushes X to the left, X pushes Y to the right, which is why Y accelerates from rest to the right.
